# Turnover v1.5.2 Release Notes
A bug-fix and polish update: keyboard control for the whole app, roles in Timeline Index+, a steady preview playback, and a simpler, shape-safe Resolution for Data Burn-In exports.
## Keyboard
- **Cmd-1 to Cmd-9 open the tools**, in sidebar order (1 Conform Prep ... 9 Title <-> Caption); **Cmd-[ and Cmd-]** step to the previous or next tool. - **Cmd-R** runs the tool, **Shift-Cmd-R** sends the result to Final Cut Pro, **Cmd-K** opens the Burn-In Customizer, **Cmd-E** exports the video, **Cmd-.** stops the current export. A new **Tools** menu lists them all; commands that cannot be used yet are grayed out. - **Customizer:** a new **Element** menu with Cmd-N (new element), Cmd-D (duplicate), Option-Cmd-Delete, Shift-Cmd-H (hide/show), Option-Cmd-Up/Down (reorder) and Option-Cmd-1 to 4 for the Element, Display, Data and Export settings. Up/Down select the previous/next element, and **Option plus an arrow nudges the selected element by a pixel** (Shift as well for ten). Cmd-key combinations now always reach the menus; before, a few of them (such as Cmd-O) were taken by the preview's single-key controls while the Customizer was open. - **Timeline Index+:** Cmd-F goes to the search field, Down arrow from there goes to the list, Return moves the playhead to the selected clip again. - Tab and Shift-Tab move between controls; macOS needs **Keyboard navigation** switched on (System Settings > Keyboard) for Tab to reach every button and menu.
See [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://github.com/wtembundit/Turnover/blob/main/docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md) for the full list.
## Timeline Index+
- **A Role column**, with each clip's Final Cut Pro role as Final Cut writes it (Video, Titles, VFX, Adjustment Clips, Dialogue, Dialogue.BoomMic ...) and a small square in **Final Cut's own colour** for it. Custom roles show under the names you gave them. A sync clip's single audio channels (Camera, BoomMic, Mix ...) are in the tooltip and the detail panel. - **A Role filter** laid out like the Roles list in Final Cut's own Index: video roles, then audio roles, each with its colour. A role with sub-roles opens them as a sub-list instead of making the list long: pick **All Dialogue** for the main role with everything under it, or a single sub-role. Only the roles of the open project are listed. - Sub-roles are read from every audio channel of a clip, including the channels synced in from a separate recorder (BoomMic, MixL, MixR-1 ... Namphet, Yak), and follow Final Cut's own rules: a muted or switched-off channel of the clip itself does not count, and a channel's role overrides the clip-level audio role. On the test project the video roles, the audio roles and all the Dialogue sub-roles match Final Cut's Index Roles list one for one. - The first filter is now called **All Effects** (it was a bare "All"), and its column **Effects / Changes**, so each of the three filters says what it chooses: effects, types, roles. The CSV export keeps its "Features" column name. - The search field also matches role names. - The CSV export has two new columns, **Role** and **Audio Channel Roles**.
## Data Burn-In
- **Playback in the Customizer is steady.** Without a reference video, Play moved one frame on every tick of a 60-per-second timer, so a 24 fps project ran at about two and a half times speed and stuttered: the burned-in text and timecode changed so fast that the bottom of the preview seemed to shake. It now follows the real clock at the speed you pick (1x, or J/L for faster), and stops at the end it is travelling towards. - **Deselect by clicking the picture.** A click on the preview, away from any element, takes the orange frame off, so you can judge the burn-in without it (a click on an element or its row in the list selects it again; Shift-Cmd-A does the same). - **Full screen preview.** A new button at the right of the transport bar (or **F**, or Shift-Cmd-F) puts the preview alone on the whole screen, with the transport bar under it, to check the burn-in at full size. F, Esc or the button brings the panels back. No element frames are drawn there, and the burned-in text is redrawn at once for the new size (it used to stay small until you scrubbed, both entering and leaving full screen). - **Resolution is one choice, not two.** The export menu used to mix percentages with named sizes (1080p, 720p ...), which went wrong for pictures that are not 16:9. Now it is **Original**, a percentage (200%, 150%, 75%, 50%, 25%) or **Custom**, and every choice scales both edges together, so the picture keeps its shape: portrait stays portrait, 4:3 stays 4:3, 2.39:1 stays 2.39:1. Each menu entry shows the size it gives for your picture, and the line under it states the result and its shape ("1280 x 720, 16:9"). - **Custom** takes a width or a height, whichever you type; the other edge follows. The estimated file size follows too. - Presets saved with the old named sizes (such as 1080p) still work and mean the same as before. The command-line option `--resolution` accepts `original`, a percentage, `w1280`, `h720` or `1080p`, and `--burn-in-transparent` accepts it too.
## Notes
Only the Standalone app and its Timeline Index+ panel changed. The Final Cut Pro side of Timeline Index+ (the permission prompt on first use, opening Turnover once from the Applications folder) is as in v1.5.1.

# Turnover v1.5.1 Release Notes
A small update: one Data Burn-In fix, and the Timeline Index+ fixes from v1.5.0 for anyone who installed the first v1.5.0 download.
## Read this if Timeline Index+ stays on "Loading..."
For about nine hours on 22 October the v1.5.0 download was a first build that did not yet contain the two Timeline Index+ fixes listed in the v1.5.0 notes. On that build the panel stays on "Loading..." (or says "No active project") on Macs with System Integrity Protection on, which is every normal Mac. It was replaced under the same version number, so Turnover could not tell the two apart. **v1.5.1 contains the fixes**: if you installed v1.5.0 that day, update now.
- Turnover > Check for Updates... offers v1.5.1. Or download it from the release page and replace Turnover in the **Applications** folder. - Open Turnover once from the Applications folder, then reopen Final Cut Pro. - The first time you open Timeline Index+, macOS asks whether Turnover may control Final Cut Pro: choose **Allow**.
## Data Burn-In
- **Missing connected layers.** A clip connected above the primary storyline was left out of the burn-in (its video track and timecode never appeared) when it was a synced clip that is itself retimed and holds its own clips inside. All such layers now show, with the right source timecode and retime, and numbered by video track like the others (V2, V3...). - A connected synced clip that shows only part of a longer clip inside it now follows its own window on the timeline. It could previously appear to run for as long as the clip it sits on.
## Notes
Only the Standalone app changed. Timeline Index+ is the same as in v1.5.0 apart from the installation problem above.

# Turnover v1.5.0 Release Notes
Turnover v1.5.0 is a big update to the Standalone app: a redesigned window, automatic updates, a much more flexible Data Burn-In, VFX tools that work with captions as well as titles, a round of Conform Prep fixes, and a long list of Timeline Index+ accuracy fixes. The SpliceKit plugin is no longer part of Turnover.
## Updating
- **This is the first version that updates itself.** Turnover now checks for new versions in the background and installs them from the app menu (Turnover > Check for Updates...). Copies older than v1.5.0 cannot do this, so install this one by hand: download it from the release page, move Turnover to the **Applications** folder, and open it from there. - Requires a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later. - The SpliceKit edition and its Lua tools have been retired. Everything they did is in the Standalone app.
## The new window
- A sidebar with two tabs, **Turnover** and **VFX**, each listing its tools. The FCPXML you are working on sits at the top of the sidebar, because every tool uses the same file; drop a file anywhere in the window to replace it. - All settings live in the main window, with the Liquid Glass look on macOS 26. - Run, Send to Final Cut Pro and the other actions are laid out the same way in every tool.
## Data Burn-In
**A cache-first flow.** Build the Burn-In cache first; Customize, Reference Video and Export unlock once it is ready. Building no longer pops the Customizer open.
**A redesigned Customizer.** - A burn-in is a list of independent **elements**. Add, duplicate, delete, show or hide and reorder them, and drag them anywhere in the preview (they snap to corners and the centre). Offsets are fractions of the frame, so a preset looks the same at any resolution. - Global style and per-element style are separated: an element can follow the global look or have its own size, colour and padding. - Undo and redo for every change, reset buttons for Move across / Move down, labels that are never cut off.
**Export.** - **Resolution:** scale an export up or down (200%, 150%, 75%, 50%, 25%, or 2160p to 360p) while keeping the picture's aspect ratio. Text and padding scale with the picture. - Burned-in **ProRes 422** (HQ, standard, LT, Proxy) is available again, with PCM audio. - Fixed an export that could freeze part-way through when the picture was ready before its audio.
**Connected layers, without extra data items.** Each element can repeat its own text for every connected layer, stacked away from the frame edge: file, timecode, metadata **and analysis** (retime, transform, crop...) come from that layer's own clip. A blank line separates the groups, and an optional label names each by its video track: V1 for the primary storyline, V2 for a clip connected on lane 1, V3 for lane 2. The older Source Layers list items still exist and are now labelled as a separate feature in the Display tab.
**Captions as data.** Caption text, role, name and VFX number/note are available to any element. Choose which caption roles an element reads (SRT, iTT, CEA-608, any role name) to burn in subtitles or to show VFX shots, with the element's own font, size, colour and position. Captions switched off in Final Cut Pro are skipped unless you turn on "Include disabled captions" for that element.
**More accurate source data.** - Clips with a Conform Rate (for example 23.98 or 47.95 material in a 24p project) now advance one source frame per timeline frame, as Final Cut Pro does, so source timecode no longer drifts on long clips. - Fixed shots that had no source data at all: a retimed Synchronize Clips item whose picture sat inside it. - Clip starts are matched with a small tolerance so a clip's first frame is never taken for the previous clip. - Fixed a clip missing from Data Burn-In when it had an unrelated connected item nested inside it, a retimed clip inside a sync clip not showing its Speed, connected layers collapsing when two stacked layers shared a source position, and a connected sync insert showing the take's full length instead of its short placed window.
## Conform Prep
Conform Prep flattens a project for conform: sync clips, and the common kinds of multicam clip, become plain video-only clips that reference the original media, with retimes, titles, markers and effects kept.
- A hold at the head of a retimed clip, and the speed ramps after it, are kept. - Captions inside a sync clip stay with the flattened clip, and sync clips whose extras are captions or connected picture layers now flatten. - Multicam clips with stacked speeds (a retime on the multicam clip plus one inside the angle) multiply correctly, and the result imports into Final Cut Pro: very large time fractions that made Final Cut drop clips are trimmed and rounded. - Fixed a crash on projects graded with certain colour tools, and a connected clip on its own lane being dropped. - The guide now lists exactly which multicam shapes are flattened and which are skipped and reported (multicam inside compound clips, nested multicam, angles that are sync clips).
## VFX tools: captions as well as titles
VFX shots can now be carried by Final Cut Pro captions, not only by the `VFX NAMING` title.
- **VFX Source setting** in VFX Naming, Auto Marker and the other VFX tools: **Auto** (default) uses whichever the project has, or choose **Titles** or **Captions**. - **VFX Naming** (auto number and reset) reads and rewrites VFX captions the same way it does titles, and checks the result against the FCPXML DTD. Ordinary dialogue or subtitle captions are left alone. - **New tool: Title <-> Caption** (VFX tab) converts VFX titles to captions or captions to titles, in place at the same position. You choose what happens to the originals: keep them, disable them, or delete them. - **VFX Auto Marker** creates markers from VFX captions as well as titles, and its "rename and add notes" option is now on by default. - **VFX Shot List and VFX Pull EDL** pick up each shot from a marker placed anywhere inside its title or caption, whatever the marker is called, and share one definition of what a VFX shot is, so their shot lists always agree. - **VFX Timeline** reads the VFX number from captions too.
## Timeline Index+
Checked row by row against Final Cut Pro's own Timeline Index export of a complex project: every row now matches in name and position. - A transition no longer pushes the clips after it later, and transitions are listed. - Sync clips on the primary storyline use their own position instead of an audio clip connected inside them. - Connected storylines, and the clips inside them, no longer start late by the length of their connect point. - Connected clips report their real position after trimming or slipping; clips whose audio was detached and replaced by a gap are listed; internal placeholder gaps are not; animated Transform values read as one line per property. - **Works on every Mac.** The panel could stay on "Loading..." or say "No active project" on Macs with System Integrity Protection on (the default). Both causes are fixed. The first time you open it, macOS now asks whether Turnover may control Final Cut Pro: choose **Allow**. - **Setup help:** Final Cut Pro only lists the extension once Turnover has been opened from the Applications folder. Turnover warns in its sidebar when that is not the case, and registers the extension when it can. - The panel has a **Copy Diagnostics** button that records what it did and what Final Cut Pro answered, to make problems reportable, and says so when Final Cut has not sent a project. - Covers the Final Cut Pro Trial as well as the regular app.
## Known limits
- Multicam flattening still skips the shapes listed above. - Retimed clips that also carry a Conform Rate use their time map as is in Data Burn-In.
